task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-14, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Any teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR (sequential play-type pairs)
methodological_questions: Is 'drive preceding a PNR' defined within the same possession (drive then PNR then outcome) or across consecutive possessions?
Are DRIVE and PNR labels reliable enough, given foul-ending leakage and low initiation_type mapping?
How can the exposure window be defined without outcome-derived labels or lookahead?
How can confounding by lineup, player quality, opponent and game state be controlled?
Are there enough drive-then-PNR possessions for useful power, and is 'any teammate' too broad to test?

historical_evidence.finding: Labeling audit: OTHER has 36% foul endings with inflated PPP (FOUL_BUCKET); DRIVE sits 12pp below the foul benchmark (FOUL_LEAK); PNR shows a 22% foul rate; only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) map to a real play type via initiation_type. Verdict recorded: artifact_found.

Sequential pair premium and defensive aftershock: after the opponent runs play type X, the next offensive play type Y scores above its baseline. Aftershock replicated 8/8 play types in all games and playoffs (e.g. PNR +0.127, n=51,194 all-games; DRIVE +0.123, n=57,621). [prior work] is limited by small sample ([prior work]).

Play-by-play-derived shot-level PNR rates by team (e.g. OKC 7.567%, IND 13.824% of half-court shots in 2024-25) served as a calibration input for PBPProxyPNR. [prior work] shows no pass/fail gate, and calibrated PNR is later logged at ~17.9-19.6% of possessions.
Superstar suppression profiles including sequential triggering by preceding opponent play types: rank-1 deltas mostly within 1-2 SE with no multiple-comparison control; OTHER artifact flagged.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Comparing play-type PPP at face value as real efficiency differences, and mapping possessions to play types via initiation_type
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact: foul-ending shares inflate or deflate PPP by label (OTHER, DRIVE, PNR), and initiation_type maps only 0.7% of possessions to a real play type.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking sequential-trigger effects per player across many cells
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as inconclusive: deltas within 1-2 SE with no multiple-comparison control.

evidence_establishes: Per [prior work][prior work], play-type PPP comparisons involving DRIVE and PNR labels were found to be affected by foul-ending leakage, and the initiation_type mapping covers only 0.7% of possessions.
Per FAM:[prior work], a sequential effect of the opponent's preceding play type on the next offensive play type's PPP was recorded as supported, with a limited-sample caveat.
Per [prior work][prior work], subgroup sequential-trigger effects for star players were recorded as inconclusive.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests whether a teammate's own preceding DRIVE (same team, same possession) changes PNR PPP.
No retrieved record gives a corrected, foul-adjusted DRIVE-then-PNR effect size or a count of such possessions.
No retrieved record validates the possession-level DRIVE and PNR labels against video or tracking data.
FAM:[prior work] concerns the opponent's preceding play type, not a same-team DRIVE before PNR, so it does not transfer directly.
own_inferences: The hypothesis is worded as universal ('any teammate DRIVE'), which a single average effect cannot establish and which is falsifiable only as a mean-effect claim.

A DRIVE followed by a PNR within one possession probably selects possessions where the first action failed to produce a shot, which could shift PNR PPP in either direction through selection rather than causation.
If drive-then-PNR possessions are rare or contain a disproportionate share of foul endings, a naive PPP difference would be largely artifactual, as in [prior work][prior work].
Play-by-play does not directly record PNR screens, so the PNR label is a proxy; the proxy may itself be defined from preceding drive-like events, creating circularity.
Drive-kick-initiated possessions probably differ systematically in personnel, defence and clock, which are confounders.
uncertainties: Number of possessions with a labeled teammate DRIVE immediately before a labeled PNR is unknown.
How the PNR and DRIVE labels are constructed in [source] database is unknown, including whether they use any outcome information.
Whether the 0.7% initiation_type mapping applies to the current graph version is unknown.
Whether the DRIVE-then-PNR ordering is observable within possession at the event level is unknown.
Retrieved records are from earlier project work; their data versions may differ from the current data.
Whether 2025-26 data being partial on the question date matters depends on the sample freeze.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history, I would have treated this as a direct sequential-effect test. [prior work][prior work] recorded an artifact verdict for DRIVE/PNR PPP caused by foul leakage and very low label mapping, so I now require foul-neutral outcomes, label audits and a precise exposure definition before any inference. FAM:[prior work] and [prior work][prior work] show that sequential effects have been studied but only for opponent sequencing, and subgroup effects were inconclusive without multiplicity control. The decision moved from proceed to proceed_with_changes.

blocking_constraints.text: DRIVE and PNR labels are derived from play-by-play without direct screen events; the recorded audit found only 0.7% of possessions map to a real play type via initiation_type, so exposure and outcome labels may be wrong.

Foul endings were found to inflate or deflate PPP by label ([prior work][prior work]), so labels that depend on how a possession ends make PPP comparisons circular unless the outcome is defined independently of the label.
Drive-then-PNR sequences in the same possession may be rare, particularly by team, player or opponent, limiting power for 'any teammate' and subgroup claims.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved family tests the same-team drive-before-PNR hypothesis. FAM:[prior work] (supported) addresses opponent play-type sequencing, [prior work][prior work] (artifact) warns that DRIVE/PNR PPP is label- and foul-contaminated, [prior work][prior work] (inconclusive) shows the multiplicity problem in sequential subgroup analyses, and [prior work][prior work] (not a hypothesis test) only calibrated PNR rates.

risks.text: PNR and DRIVE labels are proxies from play-by-play with weak validation; misclassification may be differential by team or era.
Foul-ending leakage (PNR 22% foul rate, DRIVE below the foul benchmark) can generate apparent PPP differences purely from labeling.
Drivers, lineups, opponent defence, clock and score affect both the probability of a prior drive and PNR efficiency.
Conditioning on a possession that continued from a drive to a PNR selects on a failed first action, so the comparison group is not exchangeable.
Defining the PNR as occurring after a drive, or the possession label using later events, can use information that is only known after the exposure.
Few drive-then-PNR sequences may exist per team, player or season, so subgroup tests have low power.
'Any teammate' invites per-player or per-team slicing, and [prior work][prior work] shows the problem of uncorrected sequential cells.
The effect size on PPP is probably small relative to possession-level noise (about 1.1 points SD), so a few thousand sequences may be required.
Four seasons of play-by-play may differ in labeling, pace and the extent of PNR usage.

design.estimand: Average within-possession difference in points per possession for PNR possessions with a preceding same-team DRIVE (by a player other than the PNR ball handler, within a fixed window of 8 seconds or fewer before the PNR) versus matched PNR possessions with no preceding drive. The foul-excluded PPP (points on non-foul-ending possessions) is the primary outcome, and the all-possessions PPP is secondary. The claim 'any teammate' is tested as a pooled average plus a pre-specified heterogeneity check by drive-initiator role, not as a universal claim.
design.unit: Half-court PNR possession (graph-database derived), nested within game, team and lineup.
design.sample: Seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs, frozen as of the registration date. The partial 2025-26 data is held out as a pre-registered confirmation set only after it is complete (regular season complete 2026-04-13, playoffs complete 2026-06-21). Exclude garbage time, transition-originated possessions, and possessions with fewer than 6 seconds on the clock.
design.power: Before the outcome is examined, count eligible exposed and unexposed PNR possessions. Using a possession SD of about 1.1, a 0.05 PPP difference at 80% power needs roughly 15,000 exposed possessions per group; with clustering on team-game, a design effect of about 1.1-1.3 is assumed. If the exposed count is below the required threshold or below 3,000, report the minimum detectable effect and stop at an estimation-only report rather than a hypothesis test.
design.controls: Mixed-effects or regression with a ball-handler random effect and fixed effects for offensive lineup, opponent team, season, period, shot-clock at PNR start, score margin, and home status; pre-specify a matched or inverse-probability-weighted version with exposure propensity from these covariates. Audit labels on a hand-reviewed sample of at least 300 sequences for precision of DRIVE and PNR and report misclassification. Define exposure strictly from events before PNR start so no later information enters the label.
design.falsification: Placebo exposures: (1) the drive is replaced with a non-drive event (such as a dribble handoff or pass) at the same timing; (2) the exposure is shifted to follow the PNR; (3) pre-drive-window outcome for non-PNR actions. Also run the foul-neutral outcome, and a check that the effect disappears if foul-ending possessions are reassigned. Supported only if the main effect survives both foul-neutral and placebo checks.
design.multiplicity: One primary confirmatory test (foul-excluded PPP, pooled). Secondary tests (all-possession PPP, initiator role, season) are labeled exploratory and corrected with Holm or Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery control at 0.05. No per-player or per-team slicing is confirmatory.
design.decision_rule: Supported if the pooled foul-excluded PPP difference is positive with a 95% CI excluding 0, the point estimate is at least 0.03 PPP, the sign is consistent across at least 2 of 3 seasons, the placebo checks show no comparable effect, and the label audit shows precision of at least 85%. Rejected if the 95% CI lies entirely within +/-0.02 PPP with adequate power. Artifact if the effect appears only in the all-possessions PPP and vanishes in the foul-neutral outcome or placebo. Otherwise inconclusive.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game play-by-play and the derived play-type possession graph as of 2026-06-14, with graph build hash and label-rule version recorded. 2022-23 to 2024-25 are frozen; 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) is a held-out confirmation set; 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21) excluded from the primary analysis.
